Isolated client tests and all inherited scenarios pass in the same 83-test build.

discovered_risks: Timestamp ordering at session-registration boundaries must remain explicit; events preceding registration correctly stay unknown.
Endpoint Security exact provenance is intentionally outside this increment, so workspace-only task impact remains inferred.
Current stdio request handling is sequential; cancellation checks bound connector IPC, but a later notification cannot preempt an already-blocked request in the same line-oriented process.

evidence: The current candidate builds under Swift 6 on macOS and all 83 tests pass in one suite.
Fresh isolated Codex and Claude configurations discover the shared stdio connector; no live personal configuration is used.
A built-connector transcript discovers seven read-only tools, explains one retained event, correlates it only to the unique active task as inferred, and emits a bounded sanitized result.
MCP inline export and direct app-service export contain equal summary and event detail for the same requested range and basename privacy mode.
The inventory contains no destructive tool, cleanup candidates explicitly require review, an attempted delete_file call is rejected, and static inspection found only warning-language matches.
After the private socket is stopped, the connector returns app_unavailable, a retry/recovery instruction to open Disk Steward, and no query result.

The independent test refreshes the compact status model, exports a snapshot, and repeats left/right click routing plus Export, Settings, About, and Quit labels; inherited monitoring/export tests also pass.

Exact forbidden keys are absent, output stays below 4 MiB, the connector never opens SQLite, session IPC uses a private current-user socket, and client upgrades/uninstalls preserve unrelated configuration and evidence.
